name: Changelog
title: Changelog
summary: Releases as an ordered list, each kind named in words, with real dates and nothing behind a disclosure.
description: What changed, in an order a screen reader can count.
how: The kind is a word — Added, Fixed, Removed — not a coloured dot, and nothing is behind a disclosure: a changelog people have to expand release by release is one nobody reads.

name: Notification list
title: Notification list
summary: Every mark-as-read button named with its own item, unread said in words, and a count that stays in step.
description: An inbox where every button says what it acts on.
how: Each button is named with the thing it acts on — "Mark as read: Build 4812 failed" — because five buttons all called "Mark as read" is exactly what a screen reader would otherwise read out.

name: List with row actions
title: List with row actions
summary: A table whose per-row buttons are each named with their row, so nine buttons have nine names.
description: Rows of records, each with actions that say what they act on.
how: Every action is named with its row, and the row's name is a th with scope=row, so a screen reader says the record alongside each cell it reads.

name: Order tracker
title: Order tracker
summary: Where it has got to, said in one sentence first, then a list of stages each with its state in words.
description: An order's progress, read out rather than drawn.
how: Where the order is is said in one sentence before the list — the answer most people came for — and each stage's state is a word, never the tick or the colour alone.

name: Invoice summary
title: Invoice summary
summary: Lines, subtotal, tax and total worked out in whole pennies, in a table whose footer is a real tfoot.
description: Numbers that add up, and say what they are.
how: Every total is worked out from the lines in whole pennies — in floating point 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, which is how invoices end up a penny out.

name: Article card
title: Article card
summary: One link per card and it is the title, with the whole card clickable through that link rather than a second one.
description: A card that gives a screen reader one link, not two.
how: One link per card, and it is the title: a card with a "Read more" as well gives a screen reader two links to the same place, one of them called "Read more".

name: Author byline
title: Author byline
summary: Who wrote it and when, with both dates said, rel=author on the link, and no misused address element.
description: A byline that says published and updated.
how: Not an <address> element — that is for the contact details of the nearest article — and both dates are said, because replacing published with updated hides a fact people look for.

name: Image gallery
title: Image gallery
summary: Figures in a list, with empty and described alt treated as the different things they are, and space reserved before loading.
description: Pictures with captions, and alt text taken seriously.
how: An empty alt and a missing alt are not the same thing: empty says skip this, missing makes a reader announce the file name. A caption is not a substitute for either.

name: Click-to-load video
title: Click-to-load video
summary: No request to the video host until you press play, a button named with the video, and a titled frame.
description: An embed that costs nothing until it is asked for.
how: Nothing is requested from the video host until the button is pressed — no script, no cookie, no frame — and the frame that appears is titled, which most embeds are not.

name: Pull quote
title: Pull quote
summary: The attribution in a figcaption rather than inside the quotation, and cite used for the work, not the person.
description: A quotation whose markup says who said it, correctly.
how: The attribution goes in the figcaption, not inside the blockquote — that would make the speaker's name part of what they said — and <cite> wraps the work, never the person.

name: Team grid
title: Team grid
summary: People as a list rather than a stack of headings, with initials instead of photographs and nobody invented.
description: Who is on the team, without polluting the page outline.
how: A list of people, not a grid of headings: twelve names as h3s puts twelve entries in the page's outline that nobody wants to navigate by.

name: Logo wall
title: Logo wall
summary: Names as text when there is no image, alt that is the name rather than the word logo, and no borrowed endorsements.
description: A row of names, said properly.
how: Each alt is the name — never "… logo", since a screen reader already says image — and with no file set the name is simply text, because a wordmark is a picture of a name.
